channel.title: Sunward
channel.description: Only good news. Each morning Sunward reads real newsrooms, keeps the stories where something got better, and says why in one line.

item.title: Islands Near Portugal Turn Off Lights to Protect Seabird Fledglings Every October – 30k Already Saved
item.description: Corvo switches off its lights each October, and 30,000 seabird chicks have made it safely to sea. Evidence: Proven at scale. How you can help: Switch off outdoor lights at night in autumn to help young seabirds and migrating birds. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: How yesterday's waste is becoming tomorrow's fashion
item.description: Big shoe and fashion brands are making more products from recycled materials. Evidence: Proven at scale. How you can help: Repair or resell shoes and clothes before buying new ones. Source: BBC Science & Environment.

item.title: Glowworms Shine Again in the UK from Larvae Reared Pro Bono in Garden Shed
item.description: A volunteer breeding glowworms in his garden shed has brought their light back to UK sites. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: Leave a patch of garden unlit and unmown so glowworms and other insects can breed. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: A simple supplement may help clear brain fog after cancer
item.description: A natural molecule helped breast cancer survivors clear lingering brain fog and fatigue in a UCLA study. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: NASA reveals bold new plan to return astronauts to the Moon in 2028
item.description: NASA has a faster plan to land astronauts on the Moon in 2028, with a test flight in 2027. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Hidden climate superpower: Why some ocean “snow” carries six times more carbon
item.description: Stickier marine snow can carry six times more carbon to the deep ocean, refining climate models. Evidence: Early research. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: An ancient ocean full of giant predators reveals a surprising twist in evolution
item.description: Fossils in Colombia reveal an ancient ocean far richer in giant predators than expected. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Dogs Can Sniff-Out Invasive Plant Species With High Accuracy to Curb Their Destruction
item.description: Trained sniffer dogs in Germany found invasive plants with high accuracy, helping catch them early. Evidence: Early research. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Lucky Bird Found in Storm Drain a Mile From Home After Passing Driver Happens to Spot it Hopping in
item.description: A driver spotted a lost budgie in a storm drain a mile from home and got her back to her owner. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Baby Saved After Racing Heartbeat Detected by Family Doberman
item.description: A family dog sensed a baby's racing heartbeat, and doctors caught the condition in time. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Adventurer Finally Hugs Mom After 28-Year Walk Around the World From Home in UK
item.description: After a 28-year walk around the world, Karl Bushby is home in Hull and back with his mother. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Scientists discover Europe's ancient forests were nothing like we imagined
item.description: Europe was long open woodland and meadow, a finding that can guide how land is restored. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Rubin Observatory discovers two hidden companions of the Milky Way. Hundreds more may be waiting
item.description: The new Rubin Observatory found two unknown Milky Way companions after mapping just 7% of the sky. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: People Around the World Help Buy Royal Estate for Wildlife Conservation
item.description: Donors worldwide pooled millions to buy an estate where curlews, lapwings and rare bumblebees live. Evidence: Proven at scale. How you can help: Join or volunteer with your local wildlife trust. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Man Spends 12 Days Returning Lost Cash a Laborer Needed for His Daughter
item.description: A man in Brazil spent 12 days tracing a labourer to return the cash he needed for his daughter. How you can help: If you find lost money or property, hand it in or try to trace the owner. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: In Alaska’s capital, food comes by water, air or, most often, community sharing
item.description: In Juneau, residents feed one another through traditions of sharing fish, game and garden food. Evidence: Proven at scale. How you can help: Share surplus garden produce or food with neighbours rather than let it go to waste. Source: The Guardian Environment.

item.title: Venomous Primate Believed Extinct for 100 Years Was Hiding in Plain Sight All Along
item.description: The Bangka slow loris, feared extinct, is confirmed alive and living on its home island. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Geothermal Utilities Power Wave of US Affordable Housing with 40% Energy Savings
item.description: Vermont Gas launched a community geothermal network that cuts heating energy for affordable homes by 40%. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: Ask your energy supplier whether heat pump or shared heating schemes are offered where you live. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Scientists just found dinosaur blood that survived 115 million years
item.description: Chemically confirmed traces of blood survived 115 million years inside dinosaur bones. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Don't miss: Meteor showers, fireballs, and a supermoon light up November's night sky
item.description: November brings fireballs, a Mars and Jupiter pairing and a supermoon to look up at. How you can help: Step outside on a clear night this month to look for the supermoon and meteors. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: An anti-aging drug may help protect the brain before Alzheimer's symptoms begin
item.description: Four weeks of low-dose rapamycin improved brain blood flow in people at genetic risk of Alzheimer's. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: The butterfly effect: a brighter way to make paint?
item.description: Researchers are copying butterfly wing structures to make bright paint colours without chemical pigments. Evidence: Early research. Source: Positive News.

item.title: 400-yo Shipwreck Puzzle Finally Cracked After More Than 20 Years of Mystery
item.description: A hospital CT scanner finally revealed the workings of a 400-year-old padlock from a Welsh shipwreck. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: The Montana Ranch Where Autistic People Are Wranglers and Guides
item.description: At a Montana ranch, autistic adults work as guides, wranglers and cooks. Evidence: Proven at scale. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: Seabirds See Miracle Recovery After Avian Flu Wiped Them Out
item.description: Sandwich terns have rebuilt a south coast colony three years after bird flu wiped it out. Evidence: Proven at scale. How you can help: Keep dogs on leads near beach nesting birds in spring and summer. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Scientists solve 30-year-old mystery and discover a hidden defense against inflammation
item.description: Scientists found a defence that shields healthy cells from inflammation, a lead for new treatments. Evidence: Early research. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Personalized brain therapy hits 68 percent remission for PTSD
item.description: A newly FDA-cleared personalised brain therapy put 68% of PTSD patients in trials into remission. Evidence: Proven at scale. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: Brazil Expands Protected Area for ‘One of the Richest and Most Sensitive Biomes on the Planet’
item.description: Brazil enlarged Pantanal Matogrossense National Park by more than a quarter, protecting rich wetland. Evidence: Now policy. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Student-run Automotive Shop Opens to the Public in Houston Where Every Oil Change Helps the Next Generation
item.description: Houston high schoolers opened a public auto shop where every oil change funds their training. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Woman Becomes First Person to Swim the Entire California Coastline
item.description: Catherine Breed became the first person to swim the full 900-mile California coastline. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Who needs a golden ticket? The race to future-proof chocolate
item.description: A student made chocolate from cocoa grown in England, testing hardier crops for a warming climate. Evidence: Early research. Source: Positive News.

item.title: Maya Higa built a wildlife sanctuary on Twitch, funded by the people who watch it
item.description: Maya Higa built a wildlife sanctuary funded by the people who watch her streams. Evidence: Proven at scale. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: Stanford scientists discovered bleached coral can heal through touch
item.description: In a Stanford lab, healthy coral helped a bleached fragment recover by touching it. Evidence: Early research. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: What if we stop treating social care like a service? This village shows the way
item.description: An English village shares care through communal living, so older residents are supported by neighbours. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: Check in on an older neighbour this week and ask what would help. Source: Positive News.

item.title: Scientists identify two overlooked skills that predict reading success
item.description: A large study shows early sound-awareness skills, not intelligence, best predict reading success. How you can help: Play rhyming and sound games with young children to build early reading skills. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: All 5 genetic “letters” of DNA and RNA discovered in a 4.5-billion-year-old asteroid
item.description: All five building blocks of DNA and RNA were found in samples from the asteroid Ryugu. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Scientists reverse liver cell aging and cut Alzheimer’s-linked protein in half
item.description: An experimental drug rejuvenated liver cells in rats and halved an Alzheimer's-linked protein. Evidence: Early research. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: NASA's Hubble and Webb discover ancient worlds that remember their past
item.description: Hubble and Webb found icy worlds beyond Neptune that still record how the solar system formed. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: The Student Exchange Program That Never Leaves the U.S.
item.description: A US exchange programme sends students to live with families in other American communities. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: Smartphones, ancient tracking skills and a future for desert lions
item.description: Namibian rangers pair phone alerts with tracking skills, helping farmers live alongside recovering desert lions. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Positive News.

item.title: Want the News to Unite People? Let Them Report It
item.description: In Akron, trained residents report on public meetings, giving neighbours free, shared local news. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: Attend a local council or school board meeting and share what you learn with neighbours. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: ‘It’s all God’s creation’: farmers continue a ‘Jewishly inspired’ agrarian tradition
item.description: A growing number of Jewish Americans are finding community through small, Jewishly inspired farms. Source: The Guardian Environment.

item.title: How to move 1,300 plants for Kew's Palm House mega makeover
item.description: Kew is moving 1,300 plants so its famous Palm House can be restored. Source: BBC Science & Environment.

item.title: First dinosaur bone from Antarctica found in a drawer
item.description: A tail bone found in a museum drawer is the first titanosaur ever identified from Antarctica. Source: BBC Science & Environment.
